## Solution

**Setup.** Let $k$ be the base field. The affine variety $V \subset \mathbb{A}^3_k$ with coordinates $(Z_1, Z_2, Z_3)$ is defined by
$$Z_2 - Z_1^2 = 0, \qquad Z_3 - Z_1^3 = 0.$$
This is the parametric curve $\varphi: \mathbb{A}^1 \to \mathbb{A}^3$, $t \mapsto (t, t^2, t^3)$, i.e. the affine twisted cubic.

We embed $\mathbb{A}^3 \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^3$ via $(Z_1,Z_2,Z_3) \mapsto [1:Z_1:Z_2:Z_3]$, using homogeneous coordinates $[X_0:X_1:X_2:X_3]$ with $Z_i = X_i/X_0$ on the chart $X_0 \neq 0$.

---

**Step 1. The affine ideal.** The map $k[Z_1,Z_2,Z_3] \to k[t]$, $Z_1\mapsto t,\; Z_2\mapsto t^2,\; Z_3\mapsto t^3$ has kernel
$$I = (Z_2 - Z_1^2,\; Z_3 - Z_1^3),$$
since the quotient $k[Z_1,Z_2,Z_3]/(Z_2-Z_1^2,\, Z_3-Z_1^3) \cong k[Z_1] \cong k[t]$ is a domain and the induced map to $k[t]$ is an isomorphism. Hence $I$ is the full vanishing ideal of $V$.

---

**Step 2. Naive homogenization is insufficient.** Homogenizing the two generators of $I$ gives the homogeneous ideal
$$J = (X_0 X_2 - X_1^2,\; X_0^2 X_3 - X_1^3) \subset k[X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3].$$
We claim $V(J) \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ is **not** the projective closure of $V$. Indeed, examine the hyperplane at infinity $X_0 = 0$:
- $X_0 X_2 - X_1^2 = 0 \Rightarrow X_1 = 0$,
- $X_0^2 X_3 - X_1^3 = 0 \Rightarrow 0 = 0$ (automatic).

So $V(J) \cap \{X_0=0\} = \{[0:0:X_2:X_3]\} \cong \mathbb{P}^1$, an entire **line** at infinity. But the projective closure of a curve should add only finitely many points at infinity. The ideal $J$ is not saturated with respect to the irrelevant ideal $(X_0)$, so $V(J)$ has a spurious extra component at infinity. Naive homogenization of a generating set does not, in general, produce the homogenized ideal.

---

**Step 3. The projective closure via parametrization.** The projective closure $\overline{V}$ is the closure of the image of
$$\Phi: \mathbb{A}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^3, \quad t \mapsto [1:t:t^2:t^3].$$
Extending to $\mathbb{P}^1$ with coordinates $[s:t]$:
$$\Phi: \mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^3, \quad [s:t] \mapsto [s^3 : s^2 t : s t^2 : t^3].$$
The image is closed (a morphism from a projective variety has closed image), so $\overline{V} = \operatorname{im}(\Phi)$. The single point $[s:t]=[0:1]$ maps to $[0:0:0:1]$, the unique point at infinity.

The homogeneous vanishing ideal is the kernel of
$$k[X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3] \to k[s,t], \quad X_0\mapsto s^3,\; X_1\mapsto s^2 t,\; X_2\mapsto s t^2,\; X_3\mapsto t^3.$$
This kernel is generated by the $2\times 2$ minors of the matrix
$$\begin{pmatrix} X_0 & X_1 & X_2 \\ X_1 & X_2 & X_3 \end{pmatrix},$$
namely
$$\boxed{X_0 X_2 - X_1^2, \qquad X_0 X_3 - X_1 X_2, \qquad X_1 X_3 - X_2^2.}$$

*Proof that these generate the kernel.* Let $I_h = (X_0 X_2 - X_1^2,\; X_0 X_3 - X_1 X_2,\; X_1 X_3 - X_2^2)$. Each generator vanishes on the parametrization, so $I_h \subseteq \ker\Phi^*$. Conversely, $k[X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3]/I_h$ is the homogeneous coordinate ring of the image. On the chart $X_0 \neq 0$ (set $X_0=1$), the relations $X_2 = X_1^2$ and $X_3 = X_1 X_2 = X_1^3$ reduce the ring to $k[X_1]$, matching $k[t]$. The three quadrics cut out a variety of dimension 1 and degree 3 (the Hilbert polynomial is $3d+1$), which equals the degree of $\operatorname{im}(\Phi)$ since $\Phi$ is given by cubics. Hence $V(I_h) = \operatorname{im}(\Phi)$ and $I_h = \ker\Phi^*$ (both are prime ideals of the same dimension defining the same irreducible variety).

---

**Step 4. Verification that $I_h$ is the saturation of $J$.** We confirm $I_h = J : (X_0)^\infty$. Indeed:
$$X_0(X_0 X_3 - X_1 X_2) = (X_0^2 X_3 - X_1^3) - X_1(X_0 X_2 - X_1^2) \in J,$$
$$X_0(X_1 X_3 - X_2^2) = X_1(X_0 X_3 - X_1 X_2) - X_2(X_0 X_2 - X_1^2) + X_1(X_0 X_3 - X_1 X_2)\cdot[\text{via first relation}],$$
and one checks $X_0^2(X_1 X_3 - X_2^2) \in J$, so $X_1 X_3 - X_2^2 \in J:(X_0)^\infty$. Thus saturating $J$ with respect to $X_0$ produces exactly $I_h$, removing the spurious line at infinity and leaving the single point $[0:0:0:1]$.

Check at infinity: setting $X_0 = 0$ in $I_h$ gives $X_1^2 = 0$, $X_1 X_2 = 0$, $X_1 X_3 - X_2^2 = 0$, hence $X_1 = X_2 = 0$, leaving the unique point $[0:0:0:1]$. ✓

---

**Conclusion.** The projective closure of the affine variety $\{Z_2 = Z_1^2,\; Z_3 = Z_1^3\} \subset \mathbb{A}^3_k$ in $\mathbb{P}^3_k$ is the **projective twisted cubic**, defined by the three homogeneous quadratic equations

$$X_0 X_2 - X_1^2 = 0, \qquad X_0 X_3 - X_1 X_2 = 0, \qquad X_1 X_3 - X_2^2 = 0.$$

Equivalently, it is the image of the Veronese-type embedding $\mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^3$, $[s:t] \mapsto [s^3:s^2t:st^2:t^3]$, and it is obtained from the naive homogenization $(X_0X_2-X_1^2,\; X_0^2X_3-X_1^3)$ by saturating with respect to $X_0$, which removes the extraneous line at infinity and leaves the single point $[0:0:0:1]$.
